subs.label: Romance
subs.axis: Axis: by the love-story engine, what draws the lovers together or keeps them apart; dramatic engines first (obstacle, suffering, obsession, betrayal, the couple itself, war, period, youth, queer love), then the comic engines of the romantic comedy, the romantic fantasy last.

leaves.label: Star-Crossed Romance
leaves.defn: A love story whose engine is an outside force forbidding the match: feuding families, class or caste, religion or ethnicity, custom, state or law (Romeo + Juliet, Bombay, Jungle Fever, Cold War). A comic treatment of the same obstacle goes to the romantic-comedy leaves; a wartime separation goes to A13-6.
leaves.aliases: forbidden love; star-crossed lovers; interracial romance film
leaves.see: A13-6 Wartime Romance; A13-7 Period Romance
leaves.axis: by the force that forbids the match: feuding families, class, faith and ethnicity, custom and state

leaves.label: Romantic Melodrama & Weepie
leaves.defn: A love story built to move the audience to tears through suffering, sacrifice, illness, death or loss (Now, Voyager, Love Story, The Fault in Our Stars, The Notebook). The tearjerker and the woman's film; an obsessive, self-destroying love goes to A13-3.
leaves.aliases: tearjerker; weepie; woman's film; sick-lit romance
leaves.see: A13-3 Amour Fou; A16 Drama
leaves.axis: by the source of the tears: sacrifice, illness, grief, lost memory, sentimental small-town romance last

leaves.label: Amour Fou & Obsessive Love
leaves.defn: A love story whose engine is the lovers' own excessive, possessive or self-destroying passion rather than an outside obstacle (Devdas, Leaving Las Vegas, Loulou, Kabir Singh). Where sex itself is the subject the title goes to A15-1.
leaves.aliases: amour fou; mad love; obsessive love; toxic romance
leaves.see: A15-1 Erotic Drama; A3 Thriller & Mystery
leaves.axis: by the form the excess takes: self-destructive devotion, possession and jealousy, lovers outside the law

leaves.label: Adultery & Love Triangle
leaves.defn: A love story driven by a third party: an affair, a betrayal of marriage, two rivals for one heart, or a temptation resisted (Brief Encounter, In the Mood for Love, Closer, My Night at Maud's). A comic triangle goes to the romantic-comedy leaves.
leaves.aliases: infidelity drama; love triangle; affair film
leaves.see: A13-5 Relationship Drama
leaves.axis: by what the third party does: a brief or unconsummated affair, adultery, the triangle, the temptation tale

leaves.label: Relationship Drama
leaves.defn: A love story with no outside obstacle whose subject is one couple's relationship itself: its chance beginning, its course over years, separation by distance, breakdown, or love late in life (Before Sunrise, Past Lives, Blue Valentine, Like Crazy). An affair or triangle goes to A13-4; a weepie of illness to A13-2.
leaves.aliases: couple drama; brief encounter; long-distance romance; May-December romance
leaves.see: A13-4 Adultery & Love Triangle; A16 Drama
leaves.axis: by the span of the relationship shown: one encounter, years, distance, crisis, late life

leaves.label: Wartime Romance
leaves.defn: A love story whose engine is war: lovers met, parted or endangered by a war that stays in the background of the romance (Casablanca, Waterloo Bridge, The English Patient, Dear John). A film about the fighting goes to A9.
leaves.aliases: war romance
leaves.see: A9 War Film; A13-7 Period Romance

leaves.label: Period Romance
leaves.defn: A love story set in a reconstructed past, where period manners, dress and social codes shape the courtship: classic novel adaptations and original period love stories (Wuthering Heights, Titanic, Far and Away, Lady Chatterley's Lover). Heritage romance; a wartime love story goes to A13-6.
leaves.aliases: historical romance; costume romance; heritage romance
leaves.see: A8 Historical & Period Film; A13-6 Wartime Romance
leaves.axis: by source: adaptation of a literary classic, then original period story

leaves.label: Teen Romance
leaves.defn: A love story whose lovers are adolescents or just past adolescence, built on first love, school and youth (Say Anything..., The Spectacular Now, To All the Boys I've Loved Before, After). Queer teen love goes to A13-9; a teen weepie of illness to A13-2.
leaves.aliases: first love film; high-school romance; new adult romance; teen romantic comedy
leaves.see: A13-9 LGBTQ+ Romance; A17 Children's & Family Film
leaves.axis: by the youth setting and tone: first love, high-school drama, teen comedy, new-adult bad-boy romance

leaves.label: LGBTQ+ Romance
leaves.defn: A love story between lovers of the same sex or across gender identity, where queer desire is the romance (Brokeback Mountain, Carol, Call Me by Your Name, Fire Island). A queer movement film of the early 1990s goes to A1.
leaves.aliases: queer romance; gay romance; lesbian romance; sapphic romance
leaves.see: A1 Movements & Schools (New Queer Cinema); A13-8 Teen Romance
leaves.axis: by the lovers and the tone: gay men, women (incl. trans women), queer first love, queer romantic comedy

leaves.label: Screwball Comedy
leaves.defn: A fast, farcical romantic comedy of verbal sparring, class mix-ups and a dominant heroine, in the 1930s–40s cycle and its later revivals (Vivacious Lady, Woman of the Year, Something Wild, Intolerable Cruelty). A quieter comedy of manners goes to A13-12.
leaves.aliases: screwball; neo-screwball
leaves.see: A13-12 Romantic Comedy of Manners; A12 Comedy
leaves.axis: by type

leaves.label: Pink Neorealism
leaves.defn: Italian 1950s romantic comedy that keeps neorealism's poor settings and non-star manner but turns them to sentimental courtship (Two Cents Worth of Hope). Neorealismo rosa.
leaves.aliases: neorealismo rosa
leaves.see: A1 Movements & Schools (Italian neorealism)

leaves.label: Romantic Comedy of Manners
leaves.defn: A witty, talk-driven romantic comedy whose engine is the social and sexual manners of a milieu, usually urban, sophisticated or literary (Ninotchka, Smiles of a Summer Night, Annie Hall, Bridget Jones's Diary). A farcical screwball goes to A13-10.
leaves.aliases: sophisticated comedy; Lubitsch touch; urban romantic comedy
leaves.see: A13-10 Screwball Comedy; A12 Comedy
leaves.axis: by milieu and source: continental sophistication, urban neurosis, Shakespeare and Austen, ensemble roundelay

leaves.label: Sex Comedy
leaves.defn: A romantic comedy whose engine is sex and the rules of dating: seduction, sexual mores, hook-ups and the failures of the dating market (Pillow Talk, There's Something About Mary, Knocked Up, How to Be Single). A teen sex comedy goes to A12.
leaves.aliases: sex comedy; gross-out romantic comedy; dating comedy
leaves.see: A12 Comedy; A13-17 Friends to Lovers
leaves.axis: by era and register: Hollywood sex comedy, gross-out romantic comedy, hook-up and dating comedy

leaves.label: Meet-Cute Romantic Comedy
leaves.defn: A romantic comedy whose engine is the contrived or fated first meeting and the near misses that follow, including courtship by letter and the romance of a trip (Sleepless in Seattle, Serendipity, You've Got Mail, French Kiss). The friends who were already there go to A13-17.
leaves.aliases: meet cute; destiny romcom; epistolary romance; holiday romance
leaves.see: A13-5 Relationship Drama (Chance Encounters)
leaves.axis: by how the lovers meet: fate and near misses, letters and screens, a journey abroad

leaves.label: Enemies to Lovers
leaves.defn: A romantic comedy whose couple begins in hostility, rivalry or total mismatch and fights its way to love (The Quiet Man, The Ugly Truth, Hum Tum, Anyone But You). Battle-of-the-sexes and opposites-attract comedy; rivals at work go to A13-19.
leaves.aliases: battle of the sexes; opposites attract; bickering couple
leaves.see: A13-10 Screwball Comedy; A13-19 Workplace Romantic Comedy
leaves.axis: by type

leaves.label: Fake Relationship
leaves.defn: A romantic comedy whose engine is a pretence: a fake engagement or marriage of convenience, a bet, a disguise or mistaken identity, or a matchmaker's scheme (Green Card, The Proposal, How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days, Hitch). A teen bet comedy goes to A13-8.
leaves.aliases: fake dating; marriage of convenience; romantic deception; Cyrano comedy
leaves.see: A13-15 Enemies to Lovers; A13-20 Wedding Comedy
leaves.axis: by the kind of pretence: fake couple, wager, disguise, matchmaking scheme

leaves.label: Friends to Lovers
leaves.defn: A romantic comedy whose engine is a friendship that turns, slowly or suddenly, into love, including the friends-with-benefits arrangement (When Harry Met Sally..., Love, Rosie, Jaane Tu... Ya Jaane Na, Friends with Benefits). A dramatic version spanning years goes to A13-5.
leaves.aliases: friends to lovers; friends with benefits; friend zone
leaves.see: A13-5 Relationship Drama; A13-13 Sex Comedy
leaves.axis: by type

leaves.label: Cinderella Story
leaves.defn: A romantic comedy whose engine is a match across wealth or rank in which one lover is raised into the other's world: makeover, royalty, celebrity (Pretty Woman, Roman Holiday, Notting Hill, Maid in Manhattan). A forbidding, tragic class divide goes to A13-1.
leaves.aliases: Cinderella story; rags to riches romance; royal romance
leaves.see: A13-1 Star-Crossed Romance
leaves.axis: by the higher world entered: wealth and makeover, royalty and power, celebrity

leaves.label: Workplace Romantic Comedy
leaves.defn: A romantic comedy whose couple meets and spars through a shared job, office or profession (Desk Set, Office Romance, Working Girl, Two Weeks Notice). Career-woman comedy; workplace enemies with no job plot go to A13-15.
leaves.aliases: office romance; career woman comedy
leaves.see: A13-15 Enemies to Lovers

leaves.label: Wedding Comedy
leaves.defn: A romantic comedy organised around a wedding: brides and planners, guests and crashers, or the clash of two families and arranged matches (Four Weddings and a Funeral, My Best Friend's Wedding, My Big Fat Greek Wedding, Band Baaja Baaraat). A wedding as one scene only does not count.
leaves.aliases: wedding film; meet-the-parents comedy; arranged-marriage comedy
leaves.see: A13-16 Fake Relationship; A12 Comedy
leaves.axis: by who drives the comedy: the couple and their wedding, the guests, the families

leaves.label: Holiday Romantic Comedy
leaves.defn: A romantic comedy built on a calendar holiday that sets its deadline and mood: Christmas, New Year, Valentine's Day (The Irony of Fate, Valentine's Day, Holidate). Christmas only as backdrop does not count.
leaves.aliases: Christmas romcom; New Year comedy
leaves.see: A13-12 Romantic Comedy of Manners (Ensemble Roundelay)

leaves.label: Romantic Comedy-Drama
leaves.defn: A romantic comedy played half-seriously, whose obstacle lies in the lovers' own eccentricity, damage, family burdens or age (Moonstruck, As Good as It Gets, Silver Linings Playbook, Something's Gotta Give). A purely dramatic treatment goes to A13-5.
leaves.aliases: romantic dramedy; seriocomic romance
leaves.see: A13-5 Relationship Drama; A16 Drama
leaves.axis: by the lovers' burden: eccentricity, damage or illness, children and second chances, age, a homecoming

leaves.label: Romantic Fantasy
leaves.defn: A love story, dramatic or comic, whose engine is a fantastic or speculative device: ghosts and afterlife, time travel, supernatural creatures, machines, magic or a time loop (Ghost, Somewhere in Time, Twilight, Her, Palm Springs). Where the device dominates and love is secondary the title goes to A5 or A6.
leaves.aliases: paranormal romance; time-travel romance; supernatural romance; science-fiction romance
leaves.see: A5 Science Fiction; A6 Fantasy & Adventure
leaves.axis: by the fantastic device: ghost, time travel, creature, machine, magic, loop or parallel life

subs.label: Musical & Dance Film
subs.axis: Axis: by how music and dance enter the story: integrated song (book musical, operetta), song as performance (revue, backstage), all-sung forms, rock and pop forms, recorded stage shows, dance, and films about musicians without musical numbers last.

leaves.label: Book Musical
leaves.defn: A musical film whose songs and dances arise inside the story and carry plot and character, written for the screen or adapted from the stage (Top Hat, Meet Me in St. Louis, West Side Story, La La Land). Numbers staged as performances go to A14-4; an all-sung film to A14-5.
leaves.aliases: integrated musical; film musical; stage-musical adaptation
leaves.see: A14-4 Backstage Musical; A14-5 Opera Film
leaves.axis: by origin and audience: Hollywood studio originals, Broadway adaptations, family musicals, teen musicals, later screen originals, other film-musical traditions

leaves.label: Operetta Film
leaves.defn: A musical film in the operetta tradition, light romantic plots in a mythical Ruritania or old Europe told through sung waltzes and duets (The Love Parade, Love Me Tonight, Naughty Marietta, Ulduz).
leaves.aliases: film operetta; Operettenfilm
leaves.see: A14-1 Book Musical; A14-5 Opera Film

leaves.label: Revue Film
leaves.defn: A plotless or nearly plotless film made of separate musical and comic numbers, the screen form of the stage revue (King of Jazz, Ziegfeld Follies).
leaves.aliases: film revue
leaves.see: A14-4 Backstage Musical

leaves.label: Backstage Musical
leaves.defn: A musical film about putting on a show, whose numbers are staged as performances within the story (42nd Street, Singin' in the Rain, The Band Wagon, Cabaret). Integrated numbers go to A14-1; a musician's story without numbers goes to A14-13.
leaves.aliases: backstager; show musical
leaves.see: A14-1 Book Musical; A14-13 Music Film
leaves.axis: by the stage: Broadway and revue, Hollywood and stardom, cabaret and nightclub

leaves.label: Opera Film & Sung-Through Musical
leaves.defn: A film entirely or almost entirely sung: a filmed or adapted opera, a sung-through screen musical, or a traditional sung music-theatre form (The Tales of Hoffmann, The Umbrellas of Cherbourg, Chunhyang, Annette). A rock opera goes to A14-6.
leaves.aliases: film-opera; opera film; sung-through musical; pansori film
leaves.see: A14-6 Rock Opera & Rock Musical
leaves.axis: by type

leaves.label: Rock Opera & Rock Musical
leaves.defn: A musical film set to rock music, a sung rock narrative or stage rock musical (Tommy, Jesus Christ Superstar, The Rocky Horror Picture Show, Hedwig and the Angry Inch). A musical built on existing hits goes to A14-7.
leaves.aliases: rock opera; rock musical
leaves.see: A14-7 Jukebox Musical; A14-5 Opera Film

leaves.label: Jukebox Musical
leaves.defn: A musical film whose numbers are previously released popular songs, often one artist's catalogue (Mamma Mia!, Across the Universe, Moulin Rouge!, Sunshine on Leith). A biopic of the artist goes to A11.
leaves.aliases: jukebox musical
leaves.see: A11 Biographical Film; A14-6 Rock Opera & Rock Musical

leaves.label: Pop Star Vehicle
leaves.defn: A fiction film built to showcase a singer or band playing a version of themselves through their songs (Jailhouse Rock, A Hard Day's Night, Purple Rain, Spice World). A concert record goes to A19.
leaves.aliases: star vehicle; Elvis musical; band film
leaves.see: A19 Documentary (concert film); A14-10 Visual Album

leaves.label: Filmed Stage Musical
leaves.defn: A recording of a stage musical as performed in the theatre, or broadcast live, rather than re-made for the camera (Hamilton, Cats (1998), Grease Live!). Weakly attested label (trade: pro-shot); a screen adaptation goes to A14-1.
leaves.aliases: pro-shot; filmed theatre; live television musical
leaves.see: A14-1 Book Musical; B16 Live Event & Sports Television
leaves.axis: by type

leaves.label: Visual Album
leaves.defn: A feature-length film made to accompany a music album, its songs strung into an impressionistic narrative (Lemonade, Dirty Computer, Black Is King).
leaves.aliases: visual album
leaves.see: A14-8 Pop Star Vehicle; A20 Experimental & Avant-Garde

leaves.label: Dance Film
leaves.defn: A fiction film whose story is carried by dance and dancers, its climaxes danced performances or competitions (The Red Shoes, Saturday Night Fever, Dirty Dancing, Step Up). A sung musical goes to A14-1.
leaves.aliases: dance movie; ballet film; street-dance film
leaves.see: A14-1 Book Musical; A14-4 Backstage Musical
leaves.axis: by the dance form: ballet and concert dance, flamenco, ballroom and social dance, disco and teen dance, street and hip-hop, striptease

leaves.label: Rumberas Film
leaves.defn: Mexican golden-age cabaret melodrama starring a rumba dancer, the rumbera (Victims of Sin).
leaves.aliases: cine de rumberas
leaves.see: A14-11 Dance Film

leaves.label: Music Film
leaves.defn: A fiction film about musicians and music-making whose music is performed in the story but which is not a musical: bands, singers, players, teachers, contests (Whiplash, Once, 8 Mile, Pitch Perfect). A biopic of a real musician goes to A11; a documentary to A19.
leaves.aliases: film about musicians; band film; music-competition film
leaves.see: A11 Biographical Film; A14-4 Backstage Musical
leaves.axis: by the music world: jazz and blues, bands and rock, hip-hop and DJ, singers and stardom, choirs and classical, family, contests last

subs.label: Erotic Film
subs.axis: Axis: by how sex drives the film and the production tradition: art-house erotic drama first, erotic thriller, then softcore and exploitation traditions, national erotic cycles last.

leaves.label: Erotic Drama
leaves.defn: A narrative film whose subject is sexual desire, practice or obsession, shown explicitly as the core of the drama (Last Tango in Paris, In the Realm of the Senses, Secretary, Fifty Shades of Grey). A love story with sex scenes goes to A13; a suspense plot to A15-2.
leaves.aliases: erotic art film; erotic romance
leaves.see: A13-3 Amour Fou; A15-2 Erotic Thriller
leaves.axis: by the erotic engine: awakening, obsession and transgression, sadomasochism, unsimulated sex, bestseller erotic romance

leaves.label: Erotic Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller whose suspense is driven by sexual desire, seduction or perversity (The Housemaid, Eyes Wide Shut, A Snake of June). A mainstream erotic thriller led by crime goes to A3.
leaves.aliases: erotic thriller
leaves.see: A3 Thriller & Mystery

leaves.label: Softcore Film
leaves.defn: A film of simulated sex made for erotic display, often in the European erotic tradition (Immoral Tales, Vampyros Lesbos, Delta of Venus).
leaves.aliases: softcore; Euro-erotica
leaves.see: A15-4 Sexploitation

leaves.label: Sexploitation
leaves.defn: A low-budget independent film made to exploit sex and nudity, from roadshow sex-hygiene films to Russ Meyer and nunsploitation (Mom and Dad, Faster, Pussycat! Kill! Kill!, Ilsa, the Wicked Warden).
leaves.aliases: sexploitation; nudie-cutie; nunsploitation
leaves.see: A18 Popular Cinema Modes; A4 Horror

leaves.label: Pink Film
leaves.defn: Japanese theatrical softcore cinema (pinku eiga) of the independent studios and Nikkatsu's Roman Porno line. Kept as an attested canon although no title in the present corpus belongs here.
leaves.aliases: pinku eiga; Roman Porno; Nikkatsu Roman Porno
leaves.see: A15-3 Softcore Film

leaves.label: Pornochanchada
leaves.defn: Brazilian erotic comedy and drama of the 1970s–80s made around São Paulo's Boca do Lixo (A Dama do Lotação).
leaves.aliases: pornochanchada
leaves.see: A15-1 Erotic Drama
